newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sibneft, Noyabrskneftegaz said mulling share swap.
newsitem.headline: Sibneft, Noyabrskneftegaz said mulling share swap.

text.p: Russia's seventh biggest oil company Sibneft is considering swapping shares in its subsidiaries for a single share in the group, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
But he dismissed speculation plans for a share-swap were behind a fall in subsidiaries' 1996 profits.

"On May 12 we will carry out an investment tender, after which there will be very good grounds to introduce a unified share...to attract investment," Sibneft press secretary Igor Khazanov told Reuters.
The government is auctioning 51 percent of Sibneft next week in an investment tender. Russia's third biggest bank, Uneximbank, which already controls oil group SIDANKO, has said it will bid.
But Sibneft subsidiary Noyabrskneftegaz said no decision on the swap was likely before next year.
"For now we're not talking about it, but if it happens it will be not earlier than 1998," said Vasily Maksimov, a member of Noyabrskneftegaz's board of directors.
Shares in Sibneft are rarely if at all traded, but Noyabrskneftegaz is traded on the Russian Trading System, and is a constituent of the RTS-22 index.
Analysts said a sharp fall in Noyabrskneftegaz's 1996 profits reflected pricing policies at Sibneft, which owns a 38 percent stake with 51 percent of voting stock in the company.

They said Sibneft could be interested in a fall in Noyabrskneftegaz's share price to effect the share swap on more favourable terms, but in fact Noyabrskneftegaz had held up well since news of the fall in profits.
Until two weeks ago Noyabrskneftegaz was strongly outperforming other oil stocks, as measured on the AKM oil and gas industry index, one analyst said.
Noyabrskneftegaz's share price slipped to $11.00 on April 25, the last time the share traded, from $13.50 on March 19, the day before the company announced 1996 financial results.

Noyabrskneftegaz said pre-tax profit fell to 149.9 billion roubles in 1996 from 445.8 billion roubles in 1995, according to Russian cash-based accounting standards, while net sales rose to 9.52 trillion roubles from 7.19 trillion roubles.

Analysts said Sibneft implemented a transfer-pricing policy last year for Noyabrskneftegaz and another subsidiary, Omsk Refinery, which effectively skimmed off profits from both companies and channelled them into Sibneft.
"The question you have to ask is what is behind this -- why is Sibneft taking profits out of its subsidiary," said one Western analyst, who asked not to be named.
But Khazanov denied that Sibneft was seeking to drive down share prices through manipulating Noyabrskneftegaz's profits.

"While implementing plans to issue a unified share there will be a swap and naturally there will be attempts to swap them at a cheaper rate," he said. "But it's unlikely that this would be connected to lower profits."

But analysts said they could not understand why the decline in the share price, which was about $8.75 in late February this year, did not correspond to the much sharper fall in profits, suggesting that investors might not be aware of the situation.

"Maybe some people have pulled out, but I would call it non-dramatic," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell oil equities analyst Steve Allen. "In a market that is this illiquid and small, if people start piling into a stock that analysts say is a good buy -- which it was last winter -- it builds on its own momentum. People stop looking at the fundamental situation."

Other analysts said investors were waiting to see what would come out of the Noyabrskneftegaz annual shareholders' meeting scheduled for May 20, but said the share price was likely to continue to fall, even if not as dramatically as profits had.

"Noyabrskneftegaz trades very thinly anyway, and people will wait until the annual shareholders' meeting on May 20 and then decide what they will do," said one oil analyst, who also requested he not be named.
"Prices will not go up again. The shares have a limited lifespan as they will eventually be turned into Sibneft shares."
